claims.claim: Cyril of Alexandria was Patriarch of Alexandria from 412 to 444.
Cyril of Alexandria was born circa 376 in Egypt.
The fragments of Cyril's Commentary on the Epistle to the Hebrews appear in various catenae, which are lists of quotations of church fathers used for pedagogical purposes.
The fragments from the catenae were collected and published in a critical edition in the nineteenth century by P. E. Pusey.
For Hebrews, the bulk of the fragmentary material comes from the Niketae Catena (perhaps thirteenth century) and the Codex Parisiensis 238 (perhaps twelfth or thirteenth century).
A complete manuscript of the Classical Armenian translation of Cyril's Commentary on the Letter to the Hebrews was found in Matenadaran depositary in Yerevan, Armenia in 2020.
The Armenian text is about 43,000 words long and covers Hebrews 1:1 to Hebrews 3:19.
Most scholars think that Hebrews 1:1 to 3:19 is all the commentary that Cyril ever wrote on this letter.
The commentary is mostly directed against the theology of Theodore of Mopsuestia, whom Cyril considered as a kind of proto-Nestorian.
The commentary is a critical source for Cyril's Christology.
